name: German Shapes From libpostal's Fixtures
description: The three German fixtures of libpostal's test_parser.c (MIT licence), each written again as an original input of the same shape: the same parts, order and punctuation, another place. Each case's source names the fixture it follows.

shapes.name: a name, street, number, postcode, place and country
shapes.description: libpostal's first German fixture: a firm's name, a street ending in -straße, its number, the postcode, the place and the country, with no commas
shapes.source: Original case written for this corpus in the shape of libpostal's test_parser.c (MIT) fixture test_de_parses (a name, a street, a number, a postcode, a place and a country, with umlauts): the same parts, order and punctuation, another place; nothing copied

shapes.name: the same transliterated
shapes.description: libpostal's second fixture: the same address with the umlauts written ae, oe, ue and ss
shapes.source: Original case written for this corpus in the shape of libpostal's test_parser.c (MIT) fixture test_de_parses (the same, transliterated): the same parts, order and punctuation, another place; nothing copied

shapes.name: the country's code
shapes.description: libpostal's third fixture: the same, with the country's code at the end and no comma
shapes.source: Original case written for this corpus in the shape of libpostal's test_parser.c (MIT) fixture test_de_parses (the same, with DE for the country): the same parts, order and punctuation, another place; nothing copied
